problem_statement: Face culling in this engine can be toggled per material, but the convention that decides which triangle winding is considered the “front” side is effectively frozen to the API default. That breaks parity with content that was authored with the opposite winding, and it shows up as wrong visibility, one-sided lighting, or post-transform surprises when the scene graph flips handedness. Introduce a first-class, documented choice of front-facing winding: surface it on the shared material type (including serialization/validation for standard materials and correct copy/clone), expose it on the abstract graphics device for code that sets state directly, and ensure the forward scene draw path and the shadow pass both apply the same value. When the renderer already compensates for negative scale by swapping which face is culled, the winding choice must stay consistent with that logic rather than fighting it. Both concrete device implementations must honor the setting at the correct level of their respective APIs (immediate GL state vs whatever object describes fixed-function rasterization on the modern backend), and any reuse of compiled GPU pipeline objects must remain correct when winding differs between draws.
problem_statement_variant: Mirrored hierarchies and certain imported meshes look fine in DCC tools but arrive ‘inverted’ here: back-face rules seem right on paper yet pixels behave as if inside and outside were swapped. Treat triangle winding as configurable rendering state tied to materials, push it through the device layer for both backends, and don’t let aggressive reuse of GPU objects silently reuse the wrong rasterization defaults.
hints: Follow where face culling is applied today from materials through to draws; graphics constants and device base types; WebGL device initial GL state; WebGPU render pipeline construction and its lookup keying; null device for tests; standard material schema validation alongside existing cull validation.
